newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croat food firm sees privatisation, listing in '97.
newsitem.headline: Croat food firm sees privatisation, listing in '97.

text.p: Croatian food processor Podravka expects to be majority privatised by the end of this year and to list its shares in Zagreb and possibly a foreign bourse, the company president said.
Podravka began radically restructuring its business under the guidance of international consultants Arthur D. Little after posting a loss of 135 million kuna in 1995.
Late in 1996 it got rid of its loss-making subsidiaries, reducing the workforce by 700.
"The next step is further privatisation...in the second half of this year," president Zvonimir Majdancic told a news conference.
He said the company was striving to adjust and focus its production and marketing strategy to future profitability to prepare for an eventual flotation probably before the end of 1997.
Small shareholders currently control some 39 percent of its equity, valued at 523.5 million German marks back in 1993.
The state privatisation agency recently transferred a five percent stake from its portfolio to another company it is trying to overhaul. The government controls the rest in Podravka.
Majdancic said the Euroepan Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) might help Podravka privatise.
"The EBRD has an interest to invest in Podravka," he said, adding it was too early to say how large a stake the bank would seek.
It had spurred the privatisation of drugs firm Pliva in 1996 by granting it a loan that was later converted into an 11-percent equity stake.
But another company source told Reuters the EBRD thought Podravka's equity was too high and it might be prepared to buy 3-4 percent in the company if its current book value was reduced.
This would happen just before an eventual flotation later on this year.
Podravka will seek a full listing on the Zagreb Stock Exchange, the source said.
"This is almost certain later on in the year. Depending on the progress of restructuring the earliest (to request a listing) might be sometime this spring," the source said.

Podravka's share price hit a record high of 375 kuna earlier this week, but it closed at 330 kuna on Thursday. The nominal value of its stock is 300 kuna. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
